problem: Existing visual navigation benchmarks either target outdoor/driving scenarios or ignore collisions (Habitat Challenge, GOAT-Bench, HM3D-OVON), or count only pedestrian collisions (HabiCrowd), so they cannot measure safe indoor reactive navigation from RGB only.
motivation: Indoor robots must avoid collisions in clutter, yet real-world data collection and evaluation of unsafe behaviour is costly and risky. A simulator-based, collision-aware benchmark with RL environments and data generators (including collision 'negative' trajectories) enables scalable training and safe evaluation.
key_idea: RVN-Bench is a Habitat 2.0/HM3D benchmark for collision-aware, sequential-goal point navigation from RGB only, with an RL environment plus expert and negative (collision-ending) trajectory dataset generators.
insight: Collision-aware evaluation makes the task much harder than collision-free PointNav: DD-PPO with RGB reaches only 0.886 SR1 and 8.7 CPK on test. Depth helps a lot (DAV2 predicted depth cuts CPK by about 59%, GT depth cuts it further), and online RL beats IL despite fewer parameters. Negative trajectories give a small gain for NoMaD, and sim-collected data improves real-world transfer (Real+Sim E(G) 1.30 vs Real 0.30).
method: Task definition: agent gets RGB history plus relative goal (x,y); discrete actions MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN ±30° / STOP; sequential N_goal=32 goals with geodesic distance 4-8 m; episode ends on collision, timeout or completion.
Collision detection: NavMesh-based; a collision is registered when the executed displacement is less than the commanded step (hard kinematic constraint, no physics), with agent radius 0.18 m.
RL environment: PointNav-style reward (goal +1.0, collision -0.1 terminal, else -Δdtg-0.01), plus a cost of 1.0 on collision for Safe-RL; 800 train / 50 val / 50 test HM3D scenes.
Expert trajectory generator: random start/goal, A* on GT occupancy map padded beyond agent radius, followed with discrete actions, recording (position, yaw, image) in GNM dataset format.

Negative trajectory generator: A* on a map padded by less than the agent radius so the path collides; records k_pre=8 steps before and k_post=6 after the collision, with the collision frame repeated after t_c.

NoMaD-Neg baseline: trains NoMaD_e on expert data and NoMaD_n on negative data, samples k=8 trajectories from each, and picks the expert trajectory minimizing the constrained reward (CoR) computed from distances to both sample sets.

Baselines: ViNT/NoMaD-PointGoal (goal image encoder replaced by a 2-layer MLP on relative goal), PPO, DD-PPO and PPO-Lagrangian with ResNet-50+LSTM, and DDPPO-DAV2 (RGB + frozen Depth Anything V2 depth).

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 + 2-layer LSTM (PPO/DD-PPO/PPO-Lagrangian/DDPPO-DAV2, trained from scratch, DAV2 frozen); ViNT/NoMaD-PointGoal (EfficientNet + Transformer, diffusion for NoMaD) trained from scratch on RVN-Bench data
setting.training_data: RL: online interaction in 800 HM3D training scenes. IL: 320k simulated expert trajectories (about 828 h; 400 per scene x 800 scenes); NoMaD-Neg replaces 6.25% with negative trajectories. Real-world experiment also uses 54 h of real data (GoStanford, RECON, SCAND, SACSON).
setting.observation: forward-facing monocular RGB 256x256 (history of frames) + relative goal position; DAV2-estimated or GT depth in variants
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT depth only in an ablation variant; GT occupancy map used only for data generation)

numbers.backbone: ResNet-50+LSTM, RGB + frozen Depth Anything V2 depth, DD-PPO
numbers.extra: 8 L40S GPUs, trained online in RVN-Bench train scenes

numbers.backbone: ResNet-50+LSTM, RGB + frozen DAV2 depth, DD-PPO

numbers.evidence: Table ablation on observation types, Test: 0.940 / 22.99 / 1.8

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 real-world episodes (15 office, 5 house), N_g=5, Jackal UGV
numbers.extra: trained on 54 h real + 828 h sim data

numbers_note: Own benchmark, so no canonical benchmark name; the table also lists other baselines (PPO, PPO-Lagrangian, ViNT, NoMaD-PointGoal) that are omitted here. The paper's ablation table shows DD-PPO RGB+Predicted Depth with E(G) 22.70 on train, inconsistent with the main table's 20.79.
results: DDPPO-DAV2 is the best baseline (test SR1 0.928, E(G) 20.79, CPK 3.6), ahead of DD-PPO (0.886/13.90/8.7) and all IL methods; NoMaD-Neg slightly improves on NoMaD-PointGoal (E(G) 4.61 vs 4.52 test). ViNT-PointGoal fails (SR1 0.093). In real-world tests, mixing sim and real data gives the best result (SR1 0.75).
limitations: Only static environments, discrete actions and NavMesh kinematic collision (no physics contact dynamics).
Real-world evaluation is small (20 episodes) and uses a single platform (Jackal UGV).
Gains from negative data are marginal, and the benchmark has no dynamic obstacles.
